title: Requirements and service boundaries
outcome: Explain requirements and service boundaries using the deciding step in this fictional service.
scenario: Museum fact desk. A visitor asks the opening year of exhibit P and asks the bot to sell a ticket.
given: Approved card P says 1912. The contract permits reading cards, not selling tickets.

steps.label: Split the request
steps.detail: Answering the year and selling a ticket are separate operations.

steps.label: Apply the boundary
steps.detail: Return 1912 with card P; do not sell a ticket.

explanation: A service boundary states permitted work; useful information does not grant extra operations.

counterfactual.change: Replace P with Q, which has no approved card.
counterfactual.prediction: The year is unsupported, and the ticket sale is still excluded.
counterfactual.reason: Knowledge and permission are separate requirements.

student_task: Split the museum visitor’s request into two operations. Which can the service perform for P, and what happens to each operation when Q has no approved card?
teacher_answer: The supplied year is 1912. Answering the year and selling a ticket are separate operations. Return 1912 with card P; do not sell a ticket. Changed case: The year is unsupported, and the ticket sale is still excluded. Knowledge and permission are separate requirements.
project_evidence: For the Grounded Learning Service, retain an annotated trace and the changed-case result. Name the contract or evidence that makes the deciding step valid, so another team can review it.
limits: An approved card can be outdated; this trace does not independently verify museum history.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice, distinct from the reserved independent case. These stipulated records illustrate reasoning; no real service execution or learner outcome is claimed.
